brief: The Fed hiked rates unanimously (12-0, +25bps) for the first time since 2023 and projected one more hike this year, which SC reads as the central bank rebuilding inflation-fighting credibility against political pressure after Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech and firmer job and inflation data plus an oil price rebound from the Middle East conflict. SC expects two more Fed hikes to 4.25-4.5% by H1 2027, fewer than the three hikes money markets price by June 2027, because SC expects disinflation as oil and tariff effects fade by Q2 2027, opening room for cuts in H2 2027. On this basis SC raises its 10-year Treasury yield forecast to 5.00-5.25% for 3 months and 4.75-5.00% for 12 months. The BoJ also hiked 25bps to 1.25%, as expected, but a 7-2 split vote raised the risk of a slower pace, pressuring JPY. The BoE held rates. SC expects the equity valuation drag from higher rates to be offset by strong 2026-2027 earnings growth and is using the dip to add exposure, staying Overweight global equities.
